newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Gulf International Bank signs $200 mln FRN.
newsitem.headline: Gulf International Bank signs $200 mln FRN.

text.p: Gulf International Bank (GIB) said on Sunday it signed a $200 million debut floating rate note (FRN) issued in international capital markets.
A bank statement said the note, which has a tenure of five years, had a coupon of 32.5 basis points per annum over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).
Bahrain-based GIB said Chase Manhattan would arrange the issue, which would be listed on the Luxembourg bourse.

"GIB intentionally chose to tap the international FRN market rather than the syndicated loan market in order to attract non-traditional term investors in the international investing community, thus opening up a much broader horizon for financing opportunities," GIB general manager Abdullah al-Quwaiz said.
GIB is wholly owned by Kuwait-based Gulf Investment Corp, which in turn is held by the governments of Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait.
